fillers.text: Belgium is a country in western Europe. It is bordered by the Netherlands to the north, Germany to the east, Luxembourg to the southeast, and France to the south. The North Sea lies to its northwest. The capital and largest city of Belgium is Brussels. Brussels is also the main administrative center for the European Union and the North Atlantic Treaty Organization. The total area of Belgium is about thirty thousand square kilometers, and the population is around eleven and a half million people. Belgium has three official languages. Dutch is spoken in the northern region called Flanders. French is spoken in the southern region called Wallonia. A small region in the east near the German border is German-speaking. Belgium is a constitutional monarchy with a king as head of state and a prime minister who leads the government. The country is known for its chocolate, waffles, beer, lace, and a wide variety of cheeses. Belgium has a long history of art, with painters such as Jan van Eyck and Pieter Bruegel the Elder. The country is also known for its medieval towns, large cathedrals, and many old market squares with detailed stone buildings.

An octopus is a soft-bodied sea animal with eight long arms. It is part of a group of animals called cephalopods, which also includes squid and cuttlefish. There are about three hundred known species of octopus. Most live in shallow ocean water, but some species are found in the deep sea. The body of an octopus has no bones, so it can squeeze through very small openings. Its arms are covered with rows of suckers that help it grip surfaces and hold prey. An octopus has three hearts and blue blood that contains copper instead of iron. It breathes through gills. When threatened, an octopus can release a dark cloud of ink to confuse predators while it escapes. It can also change the color and texture of its skin to blend in with rocks, sand, or coral. Octopuses are considered one of the most intelligent groups of invertebrates. Scientists have shown they can solve puzzles, open jars, and use tools such as coconut shells for shelter. Most octopuses have short lives. Many species live only one or two years before they die.

Carbon is a chemical element. Its symbol on the periodic table is C, and its atomic number is six. Carbon is a nonmetal. It can join with itself and with many other elements to form a very large number of compounds. There are more carbon compounds known than the compounds of all the other elements combined. Carbon comes in several different solid forms, called allotropes. The most familiar are diamond and graphite. Diamond is the hardest known natural material. Graphite is soft and is used in pencils and as a lubricant. Other allotropes include amorphous carbon, fullerenes, and carbon nanotubes. Carbon is the fourth most common element in the universe by mass. On Earth, carbon is found in the air as carbon dioxide gas, in plants and animals, in coal and oil, and in limestone rock. All known forms of life contain carbon. The study of carbon-based molecules is called organic chemistry. Carbon dating is a method used to find the age of old objects that once contained living material. It measures small amounts of a special form of carbon called carbon-fourteen.

Mount Fuji is the tallest mountain in Japan. It is located on the island of Honshu, about one hundred kilometers southwest of the city of Tokyo. Its height is three thousand seven hundred and seventy-six meters. Mount Fuji is a stratovolcano, which means it is built up of many layers of hardened lava, ash, and rock. The mountain has a nearly symmetrical cone shape and is often shown with a cap of white snow at the top. The last large eruption of Mount Fuji happened in seventeen oh seven, during a period called the Hoei eruption. Scientists still classify the volcano as active, but the chance of an eruption in the near future is considered low. Mount Fuji has been important in Japanese culture for many centuries. It is a sacred mountain in the Shinto religion. Many shrines and temples are built around its base. Each summer, large numbers of people climb to the summit to watch the sunrise from the top. Mount Fuji is also one of the most painted and photographed landscapes in the world. In two thousand thirteen, it was added to the UNESCO World Heritage list.

Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun in our Solar System. It is the second largest planet, after Jupiter. Saturn is a gas giant, which means it is made mostly of hydrogen and helium and does not have a solid surface like Earth. Its diameter is about one hundred and twenty thousand kilometers, almost ten times the diameter of Earth. Saturn is best known for its bright system of rings. The rings are made up of countless small particles of ice, dust, and rock. They range in size from tiny grains to large boulders. The ring system is very wide but very thin. Saturn has at least one hundred and forty-six known moons. The largest moon, Titan, is bigger than the planet Mercury. Titan has a thick atmosphere and lakes of liquid methane on its surface. Another moon, Enceladus, has jets of water vapor and ice shooting out from its south pole. A day on Saturn lasts only about ten and a half hours, but it takes the planet about twenty-nine and a half Earth years to orbit the Sun once.
